setup: none  -- multi-statement pins: query lines map 1:1 to ' | '-separated observed segments; observed is [tuple(row) for row in collect()]

pins.claim: Bare ORDER BY x is ASC with NULLS FIRST — the OPPOSITE default null order to DuckDB (nulls_last); the plan's mandatory explicit null order exists because of exactly this
pins.query: SELECT x FROM VALUES (2),(NULL),(1) t(x) ORDER BY x

pins.claim: ORDER BY x DESC puts NULLS LAST — Spark ties null order to direction (PostgreSQL-style), unlike DuckDB's direction-independent setting
pins.query: SELECT x FROM VALUES (2),(NULL),(1) t(x) ORDER BY x DESC

pins.claim: Explicit NULLS FIRST/LAST spellings are accepted in both directions — the printer can always force
pins.query:
SELECT x FROM VALUES (2),(NULL),(1) t(x) ORDER BY x ASC NULLS LAST
SELECT x FROM VALUES (2),(NULL),(1) t(x) ORDER BY x DESC NULLS FIRST

pins.claim: Default window frame with ORDER BY is RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING .. CURRENT ROW — agrees with DuckDB (peer rows share the running value)
pins.query: SELECT k, v, sum(v) OVER (ORDER BY k) AS s FROM VALUES (1,10),(1,20),(2,5) t(k,v) ORDER BY k, v

pins.claim: Default string ordering agrees with DuckDB's binary UTF-8 order on the same probe values
pins.query: SELECT s FROM VALUES ('B'),('Z'),('a'),('e'),('ss'),('ß'),('é'),('☃') t(s) ORDER BY s

pins.claim: <=> is the null-safe equality (the plan's JoinKey null_safe=true spelling in Spark); IS NOT DISTINCT FROM is also accepted
pins.query:
SELECT NULL <=> NULL, 1 <=> NULL, 1 <=> 1
SELECT NULL IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL, 1 IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL

pins.claim: Integer / is float division (DOUBLE) as in DuckDB; the integer-division spelling is `div` (DuckDB spells it //)
Negative integer div and % semantics, recorded against DuckDB's ((-7)//2, (-7)%2, 7//(-2), 7%(-2)) for the signature mapping
ANSI mode: integer overflow errors by name instead of wrapping — matches DuckDB's trap class
pins.query: SELECT CAST(2147483647 AS INT) + CAST(1 AS INT)
pins.observed: ERROR: [ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW] overflow. Use 'try_add' to tolerate overflow and return NULL instead. If necessary set "spark.sql.ansi.enabled" to "false" to bypass this error. SQLSTATE: 22003

pins.claim: ANSI mode: strict CAST errors on bad input, try_cast is the try form (NULL) — same strict|try split as DuckDB's CAST/TRY_CAST
pins.query:
SELECT CAST('x' AS INT)
SELECT try_cast('x' AS INT)
pins.observed: ERROR: [CAST_INVALID_INPUT] The value 'x' of the type "STRING" cannot be cast to "INT" because it is malformed. Correct the value as per the syntax, or change its target type. Use `try_cast` to tolerate malformed input and return NULL instead. SQLSTATE: 22018 | [(None,)]

pins.claim: ANSI mode: strict CAST overflow errors by name, try_cast nulls it
pins.query:
SELECT CAST(3000000000 AS INT)
SELECT try_cast(3000000000 AS INT)
pins.observed: ERROR: [CAST_OVERFLOW] The value 3000000000L of the type "BIGINT" cannot be cast to "INT" due to an overflow. Use `try_cast` to tolerate overflow and return NULL instead. SQLSTATE: 22003 | [(None,)]

pins.claim: Bare decimal literals: 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 is TRUE (DECIMAL arithmetic) — agrees with DuckDB's literal typing, disagrees over DOUBLE as everywhere
sum(DOUBLE) is order-sensitive under local[1]: same four values, permuted, different answer — Spark shares DuckDB's epsilon tier
pins.query:
SELECT sum(x) FROM VALUES (1e16),(1.0D),(1.0D),(-1e16) t(x)
SELECT sum(x) FROM VALUES (1e16),(-1e16),(1.0D),(1.0D) t(x)

pins.claim: sum(BIGINT) result type is BIGINT (errors on overflow under ANSI) — DuckDB's is DECIMAL(38,0); a printer forcing DuckDB result types must cast the argument
pins.query:
SELECT typeof(sum(x)) FROM VALUES (1L) t(x)
SELECT sum(x) FROM VALUES (9223372036854775807L),(1L) t(x)
pins.observed: [('bigint',)] | ERROR: [ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW] overflow. Use 'try_add' to tolerate overflow and return NULL instead. If necessary set "spark.sql.ansi.enabled" to "false" to bypass this error. SQLSTATE: 22003

pins.claim: TIMESTAMP_NTZ is reachable from SQL by cast — the landing zone for DuckDB's wall-clock TIMESTAMP; plain TIMESTAMP is the session-tz instant type (landing zone for TIMESTAMPTZ under pinned UTC)
